implemented: Push, checkout, clone, commit and amend enter one operation lock; confirmation and recovery stay inside that operation instead of being silently skipped by nested locking.
Non-fast-forward recovery pulls the actual tracking remote and retries the push once. Protected branches, permission errors and hook rejection never implicitly offer force-push.

History cherry-pick and request drops share stash/cancel protection, detached/unfinished-operation checks and checkout-before-cherry-pick sequencing. Request resolution rechecks the current branch after network work.
Old repository refreshes and operation errors cannot overwrite the newly selected repository. Repository changes clear old status, stash, comparison and history state.
Failed or refused amendments preserve amendment mode and the draft.
Force confirmation is bound to the branch observed before the prompt; cancelling performs no transport, and an external checkout invalidates confirmation.
Operation errors and diff-loading errors are separate: background refresh no longer clears Git failures. New guard messages are localized in English and Chinese.
adaptations: New workflow tests are project regressions, not transplanted upstream tests. Existing upstream cases and assertions are not modified.
IPC exposes native Git errors as strings, so recovery classifies the existing non-fast-forward/overwritten-file messages.
Local Git transport tests use isolated bare repositories. Native UI recovery tests intercept only the relevant transport IPC; no hosted repository writes are performed.
